newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek gold tender draws bids from 17 companies.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek gold tender draws bids from 17 companies.

text.p: Seventeen firms from Australia, Germany, Canada, South Africa and Japan have submitted bids to take part in a tender to carry out geological research on seven gold fields in Uzbekistan, an official source said.

The source in the State Committee on Geological and Mineral Resources told Reuters that the tender was announced by Uzbek President Islam Karimov during a recent visit to the United States, but U.S. firms were not among those taking part.

The interested companies include British mining group RTZ Corp Plc, Canada's Nelson Gold Corp Ltd and Teck Corp, Australia's Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) and Western Mining Corporation, the Luxembourg-based international group Minorco, Japan's Mitsubishi, and Marubeni Corp .

The tender covers fields with estimated total reserves of 1,720 tonnes of gold in the Kyzylkum and Nuratin mountain areas of the Central Asian state. The winner should be declared by February 15, 1997.
The largest gold field in the tender is Dzhetymtauskaya, with reserves estimated by the committee at 400 tonnes.
Uzbekistan will demand a minimum 50 percent stake in each of the projects, which will be tax-free for five years. But a 2.5 percent royalty on profits must be paid to the Uzbek government.
Karimov has said the desert nation has gold reserves of around 5,000 tonnes.
